name: Hindi
description: An Indo-Aryan language spoken chiefly in North India, and serves as the lingua franca of the Hindi Belt.
historicalInfo: An Indo-Aryan language spoken chiefly in North India, and serves as the lingua franca of the Hindi Belt.

name: Bengali
description: An Indo-Aryan language native to the Bengal region of South Asia.
historicalInfo: An Indo-Aryan language native to the Bengal region of South Asia.

name: Marathi
description: An Indo-Aryan language spoken predominantly by the Marathi people of Maharashtra.
historicalInfo: An Indo-Aryan language spoken predominantly by the Marathi people of Maharashtra.

name: Telugu
description: A Dravidian language native to the Indian states of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
historicalInfo: A Dravidian language native to the Indian states of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

name: Tamil
description: A Dravidian language natively spoken by the Tamil people of South Asia.
historicalInfo: A Dravidian language natively spoken by the Tamil people of South Asia.

name: Gujarati
description: An Indo-Aryan language native to the Indian state of Gujarat.
historicalInfo: An Indo-Aryan language native to the Indian state of Gujarat.

name: Urdu
description: An Indo-Aryan language spoken chiefly in South Asia.
historicalInfo: An Indo-Aryan language spoken chiefly in South Asia.

name: Kannada
description: A Dravidian language spoken predominantly by the people of Karnataka.
historicalInfo: A Dravidian language spoken predominantly by the people of Karnataka.

name: Odia
description: An Indo-Aryan language spoken in the Indian state of Odisha.
historicalInfo: An Indo-Aryan language spoken in the Indian state of Odisha.

name: Malayalam
description: A Dravidian language spoken in the Indian state of Kerala.
historicalInfo: A Dravidian language spoken in the Indian state of Kerala.

name: Punjabi
description: An Indo-Aryan language with origins in the Punjab region of the Indian subcontinent.
historicalInfo: An Indo-Aryan language with origins in the Punjab region of the Indian subcontinent.

name: Bhojpuri
description: An Indo-Aryan language spoken in the Bhojpur-Purvanchal region of India and the Terai region of Nepal.
historicalInfo: An Indo-Aryan language spoken in the Bhojpur-Purvanchal region of India and the Terai region of Nepal.

name: Maithili
description: An Indo-Aryan language spoken in the Mithila region of India and Nepal.
historicalInfo: An Indo-Aryan language spoken in the Mithila region of India and Nepal.

name: Sanskrit
description: An ancient Indo-Aryan language that is the primary liturgical language of Hinduism.
status: Once widely spoken, now mostly liturgical
historicalInfo: Served as the lingua franca of ancient India.

name: Ahom
description: A Tai language previously spoken by the Ahom people in Assam.
status: Once spoken, now extinct as a native language
historicalInfo: Was the language of the Ahom Kingdom that ruled the Brahmaputra valley.

name: Toda
description: A Dravidian language spoken by the Toda people in the Nilgiri Hills.
historicalInfo: Known for its unique phonetic system and pastoral vocabulary.

name: Great Andamanese
description: A nearly extinct language family of the Andaman Islands.
status: Once widely spoken across the islands
historicalInfo: Represent some of the oldest indigenous languages of the Indian subcontinent.

name: Santali
description: An Austroasiatic language spoken primarily by the Santal people. It has its own script called Ol Chiki.
historicalInfo: One of the most widely spoken tribal languages in India, representing the rich cultural heritage of the Santal tribe.

name: Mundari
description: An Austroasiatic language spoken by the Munda people. Efforts are ongoing to preserve it using the Mundari Bani script.
historicalInfo: Mundari is central to the identity of the Munda people and features rich oral traditions.

name: Kurukh (Oraon)
description: A Dravidian language spoken by the Oraon and Kisan tribal peoples. Tolong Siki is its recognized script.
historicalInfo: Unlike many Jharkhand tribal languages which are Austroasiatic, Kurukh is Dravidian.

name: Ho
description: An Austroasiatic language spoken by the Ho people, written in the indigenous Warang Citi script.
historicalInfo: The unique Warang Citi script was invented in the 1950s by Lako Bodra to preserve Ho cultural identity.

name: Kharia
description: A Munda (Austroasiatic) language spoken by the Kharia people. It uses Devanagari as it does not have a native script.
historicalInfo: Kharia has faced significant language shift towards dominant regional languages.
